children.title: Copying Fidelity and Compositional Stability in Evolving Prebiotic Systems

detail.title: Copying Fidelity and Compositional Stability in Evolving Prebiotic Systems
detail.summary: Evolutionary potential in prebiotic systems is governed by the interplay between copying fidelity and compositional stability. Mathematical models suggest that selection can operate on RNA populations within protocells even with stochastic replication, provided the population structure supports functional enrichment. Simultaneously, error-threshold analysis identifies explicit mutation rates (e.g., µc = 1/6 for certain cross-specific models) beyond which informational heredity degrades, establishing a clear regime for the maintenance of genetic information.
detail.reason: Notebook revision required to incorporate specific theoretical models of both RNA population dynamics and error-threshold limits.
